Hi Karthik and Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency and cost breakdown looked promising. Procurement asked me to follow up with two points before we move to a private offer: 1) recommended term lengths and corresponding discounts for a mid-sized pilot (estimated $120k ARR), and 2) how the buyer approval flow typically maps to signature windows on AWS private offers.

Our CFO wants to understand whether a 12-month vs 36-month commitment materially changes the approval chain (i.e., do we need board-level signoff for 3-year?). Procurement also wants a clear deadline for signature once the private offer link is issued so they can align internal calendars.

Can you share a few pricing/term scenarios and the approvals we should expect from your side (and any gating we should plan for on AWS marketplace)?

Julie — thanks, this is straightforward to lay out. Quick answers up front, then a suggested MOU-style plan below.

High-level term/pricing guidance (pilot ~ $120k ARR):
- 12 months: 15% off list (standard seller-led private offer rate for pilot). Fastest buyer approval (procurement + CFO).
- 24 months: 22% off list + 1 month of professional services credit. Typically requires procurement + finance signoff; sometimes CFO depending on org.
- 36 months: 28% off list + onboarding credit; often triggers executive procurement review and requires CFO signoff — recommend only if Acme wants predictable unit economics and will commit to expansion.

AWS private offer signature window and approval notes:
- We can request a 30-day signature window in the private offer metadata. That is what our sellers typically set.
- If you need shorter (14 days) we can do that but recommend 30 days to avoid last-minute procurement delays.
- For 36-month offers we usually see buyer legal + CFO review add 7-14 business days; plan for escalation path if CFO needs more time.

Suggested mutual action plan (MAP):
1) We send private offer with 30-day signature window and 12/24/36 term options (pricing matrix attached).
2) Acme confirms preferred term within 10 business days and indicates approver list (procurement contact, CFO, security reviewer).
3) DocuSign flow after private offer acceptance (we can include conditional activation if legal needs a grace period).

I'm attaching a pricing matrix I mentioned. Vanessa and I can hop on a 20-min call to walk the procurement team through approvals.

Best,

Karthik — quick legal note.

1) Signature window: 30 days is fine and the cleanest from an ops perspective. We can support 14 days on request but will flag higher risk for renewal/finance owners. Please record the signature deadline explicitly in the private offer description so procurement can track.

2) Conditional activation: we can add a clause that allows sandbox pilot access for up to 60 days prior to full commercial activation subject to an accepted SOW and an executed private offer. That reduces launch friction while keeping billing gated to signature.

3) 36-month offers: require CFO acknowledgement in writing and a standing right for us to re-price annually if AWS resale terms change materially. We'll bake that into the private offer as a discrete clause — not customer-facing but in the seller notes/attachment.

I've attached an approval routing matrix you can include in the MAP (shows who signs and typical lead times).

Priyom
Priyom Das
